source_notes: Cavanaugh, Inside Football (Boston: Small, Maynard and Company, 1919), 342-page PDF, fully text-extractable OCR layer (no image-only pages), no retraction notice (a 1919 coaching monograph). Printed text ends at printed p.318 'THE END' (PDF p.336); PDF pp.337-342 are blank back matter. Page citations in this artifact are PDF page indices (1-342) of the source file; the corresponding printed page is given in each primitive's assumptions. Purely qualitative coaching doctrine: NO equations, effect sizes, or unit-bearing quantities are printed anywhere except incidental yard/point distances and clock minutes. All six primitives are faithful predicate-logic / qualitative formalizations of printed decision rules, explicitly labeled as formalizations (no source equations exist). OCR hyphenation and quirks are preserved verbatim in every quote; quotes were verified programmatically against the whitespace-normalized source text. No sportsbook odds or betting content is quoted. Domain is football coaching history; Layer-2 mappings transfer doctrine to game-theoretic / control kernels without claiming football originated those mathematics.

primitives.name: Anti-zone-play early-offense invariant: do not gate attack by field zone; score at the earliest feasible moment; start the strongest lineup
primitives.verbatim_quote: The time to score is in the first minute of the game, if possible; if not then, in the next minute. The earlier the lead, the surer the victory and the brighter the bonfire.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: z = field-zone label (own-goal / midfield / opponent territory) [categorical, dimensionless]; ZonePlay(z) = predicate that attack is prescribed by a hard zone rule [0/1]; Predictable(z) = predicate that an experienced defender can forecast the play from zone alone [0/1]; Withhold(Offense|z) = predicate that the running/passing attack is suppressed because of zone [0/1]; t, t*_score [time, minutes of game clock]; FeasibleScore(t) = predicate that a scoring attempt is available at clock t [0/1]; Start(StrongestLineup) = deontic directive to open with the best eleven [dimensionless]. All predicates dimensionless; the only unit-bearing quantity is game-clock minutes. The invariant is the negation of zone-conditioned suppression plus an earliest-feasible-score timing rule, not a numeric optimization target (none is printed).
primitives.assumptions: Source prints prose coaching doctrine, no equations anywhere in the file; the LaTeX is a faithful predicate-logic / qualitative formalization of the printed decision rule, explicitly labeled as a formalization, not a source equation. Chapter XXXIV 'Generalship vs. Zone Play' (PDF p.287 = printed p.269). Cavanaugh argues zone play is 'an invention of coaches based on excessive, however excusable, conservatism and their distrust of their field general's good sense' (PDF p.288) and that it persists because coaches fear adverse criticism, not because it maximizes winning. Printed context: the old game was two forty-five-minute halves with infrequent substitution and possession 'considered four-fifths of the game' (PDF p.287-288); he contrasts this with the modern shorter, rest-intervaled game to rebut the energy-conservation rationale for withholding offense. Directive 'Send your quarterbacks into the game untrammeled by the superstition of zone play, and start the game with your strongest lineup' (PDF p.288). He explicitly disclaims 'senseless, indiscriminate offense' and 'hap-hazard pounding of the line' (PDF p.292): the rule is against zone-gated timidity, not against judgment.
primitives.breakdown_regime: The invariant is a policy stance, not a license for recklessness: Cavanaugh himself vetoes hap-hazard line pounding and requires each play be planned so that, perfectly executed, it should score (PDF p.292). It breaks down when the offense is genuinely outmatched in the kicking game or when early nerve-shock makes a long snap dangerous (he concedes the first kick may be justified by opening nervousness, PDF p.291). The predictability claim is empirical, not proved: a defense that does NOT assume zone play removes the exploit. The 'earliest feasible score' rule ignores clock/field-position externalities that a modern expected-points model would price; it is a 1919 doctrine, not a calibrated optimum.
timescales: tau_3: coaching career and the era's zone-play convention

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to explore-before-exploit and to policy-predictability leakage in adversarial sequential games: a zone-gated policy is a low-entropy mapping from observable state (field position) to action, which an opposing model can invert and pre-empt. Cavanaugh's remedy - ungate the attack, start the strongest lineup, score at the earliest feasible moment - is exactly the prescription to raise policy entropy early and to spend the best resources before the opponent's diagnostic model converges. The hidden motive he names (fear of criticism) is a principal-agent distortion: the coach optimizes reputation rather than win probability, the same misalignment that makes human play-callers conservative relative to an EV-maximizing engine.
layer2.telemetry: Play-type distribution conditioned on field zone and down (entropy of the zone->action map measures predictability); opening-drive scoring rate; strongest-lineup snap share in the first period; success rate of early unconventional attempts (deep pass from own half). The coach's reputation motive is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE from play-by-play alone; it is inferred from the printed doctrine, not from box-score telemetry.

primitives.name: Field-goal vs scoring-play tie-break: take the field goal only if slightly surer; at about-even chances take the big scoring play (payoff-dominance tie-break)
primitives.verbatim_quote: If it seem slightly surer than the scoring play, take the field goal. If the chances are about even, take the big scoring play.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: p_FG = subjective success probability of the field-goal attempt [dimensionless, 0-1]; p_S = subjective success probability of the deceptive scoring play (trick play / forward pass) [dimensionless, 0-1]; delta_slight = the 'slightly surer' margin [dimensionless probability gap, NOT numerically printed]; |p_FG - p_S| ~ 0 = the 'chances about even' band [dimensionless]; V_S, V_FG = payoff of a successful scoring play vs field goal [points, dimensionless counts]; V_S > V_FG encodes 'the big scoring play' (a touchdown outranks a field goal). Take = deontic selection operator [dimensionless]. The load-bearing structure is a threshold comparison plus a payoff-dominance tie-break; no numeric probabilities or point values are printed in this passage.
primitives.assumptions: Source prints prose coaching doctrine, no equations anywhere in the file; the LaTeX is a faithful predicate-logic / qualitative formalization of the printed decision rule, explicitly labeled as a formalization, not a source equation. Chapter XXXIV close (PDF p.303 = printed p.285), the decision a quarterback faces when a first down is hazardous near scoring range: choose between a stroke for a touchdown and a try at field goal. Printed antecedents: 'The efficiency of your drop-kicker is one of the factors'; 'The field goal opportunity should not be passed up unless the quarterback has an especially deceptive trick play or forward play which the coach has given him with special instructions'; 'At this stage of the game, any score puts the team scoring in the lead'; 'If the field goal is particularly sure, it is a hard thing to pass up.' The two printed branches are the formalized rule. The payoff ordering V_S > V_FG is the structural reading of 'the big scoring play' (era context: a touchdown exceeded a field goal in value); it is labeled as context, not a printed number.
primitives.breakdown_regime: The 'slightly' margin delta_slight and the 'about even' band are undefined numerically - the invariant is the decision structure (threshold + payoff-dominance tie-break), not a calibrated boundary. It breaks down when the kicker's efficiency is unknown or when the score-state changes the payoff ordering (a trailing team late may value the sure three points differently than the doctrine assumes). The rule presumes 'any score puts the team scoring in the lead', so it is a tie/lead-state heuristic, not a general expected-points policy; applying it when trailing by more than a touchdown misprices the sure field goal. Subjective probabilities p_FG, p_S are coach judgments, not measured frequencies.

layer2.mapping: Derived payoff-weighted threshold selector for the scoring-region action node of the 22-player system: choose the sure lower-payoff action only when its success probability exceeds the high-payoff action's by a margin; when probabilities are near-equal, select by payoff dominance (the touchdown). This is the general kernel of risk-sensitive action selection under a lead-state reward, and it binds as a hard decision module: an engine that always maximizes expected points without the 'about even -> big play' tie-break, or that takes the field goal whenever p_FG > p_S by any epsilon, deviates from the printed doctrine. The latent delta_slight must be carried as a tunable, era-tagged parameter, never imputed as zero.
layer2.telemetry: Field-goal success probability by distance and kicker; scoring-play (trick/pass) success probability in the same region; score-state and clock at the decision; the realized choice and outcome. The 'slightly' threshold delta_slight and the 'about even' band are LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE from outcomes alone (no numeric boundary is printed); they must be fit or declared, not read off the source.

primitives.name: Blocker single-side forcing invariant: stay on one side of the man to be blocked to collapse his dodge set to one direction; standing directly in front gives him two guesses
primitives.verbatim_quote: the way to function surely is to stay on one side of the man to be blocked, and force him to go to the other side.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: b = blocker [agent label]; m = opponent to be blocked [agent label]; Pos(b) = blocker's alignment relative to m [categorical: left side / right side / directly in front]; Side_L(m), Side_R(m) = the two lateral half-planes beside m [geometric regions]; Front(m) = the position directly ahead of m [geometric region]; DodgeSet(m) = the set of feasible evade directions available to m [set over {left, right}]; |DodgeSet| [dimensionless count, 1 or 2]. All terms are geometric regions, agent labels, or dimensionless set cardinalities; no physical units. The invariant is a choice-set reduction: lateral alignment forces a single evade direction, frontal alignment leaves two.
primitives.assumptions: Source prints prose coaching doctrine, no equations anywhere in the file; the LaTeX is a faithful predicate-logic / qualitative formalization of the printed decision rule, explicitly labeled as a formalization, not a source equation. Chapter XXXII 'Kick-off and the Run-back' (PDF p.276 = printed p.258). Printed diagnosis of the failure mode: 'the blocker inveterately places himself directly in front of his charging opponent, who is thus enabled to force the blocker to two guesses as to the direction in which he will dodge' (PDF p.276). The same invariant is printed for blocking ends under punts: 'the most important one word of instruction ... is never to allow the ends to get directly in front of them. Each should step to one side, and keep to one side, of the end, so that the latter has only a single direction in which to elude blocking' (PDF p.259). Cavanaugh adds a sincerity/incentive condition: the blocker's decisive lunge is reliable chiefly when he knows the actual ball-carrier is directly behind him and must be protected (PDF p.276).
primitives.breakdown_regime: The forcing assumes the blocker can hold his chosen side and time the final lunge; a faster or more agile opponent who reads the alignment can still beat a half-hearted block, so the geometric invariant is necessary, not sufficient - Cavanaugh stresses the blocker must be 'all as convincing in his final lunge as if he were a tackler'. It breaks down when the blocker cannot identify his man definitively (the kick-off failure mode he names is 'the individual's failure to pick out definitely the man to be blocked', PDF p.276) or when the runner abandons the prearranged path, leaving the blocker unsure whether he is driving his man into or away from the runner (PDF p.277). The two-guess frontal failure is a structural leak, not a probability estimate.
timescales: tau_1: the kick-off or punt return play
tau_2: repeated kicks across a game
tau_3: season drill of blocking assignments

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a forcing move in combinatorial game theory and to choice-set reduction in mechanism design: rather than guessing the adversary's action (a two-way guess the blocker loses half the time), the blocker constrains the adversary's feasible action set to a singleton and then commits. This is the minimax principle of removing the opponent's options instead of predicting them - the same structure as a forcing check in chess or a take-it-or-leave-it constraint that collapses a responder's strategy space. In the engine it binds as a spatial constraint on every blocking/coverage transition: alignment that leaves the opponent two free directions is a dominated action and must be pruned.
layer2.telemetry: Blocker alignment relative to his assigned man (lateral vs frontal); ball-carrier / end evade-direction distribution (a forced single direction is the success signature); block success and tackle outcomes; whether a definite man was picked pre-snap. The incentive/sincerity channel (runner directly behind) is observable from formation; the blocker's private commitment is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE except through the decisiveness of the lunge.

primitives.name: Defensive fullback nearest-central-spot covering invariant: take the minimax-central feasible spot over reachable threats; adaptive depth 25 -> 30 yards on a kick-from-running-formation
primitives.verbatim_quote: He takes the nearest central spot to all the things which may happen which are in his line and which he can get.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: x, x* = defensive fullback field position [length, yards]; theta = a possible threat event (punt landing, forward pass, long run) location [length, yards]; Theta_reach = the set of threats 'in his line and which he can get' [reachable threat set]; d(x,theta) = distance from position to threat [length, yards]; F = feasible spots constrained by InLine(x) (within his defensive responsibility) and Reachable(x) (he can arrive in time) [geometric feasibility set]; depth = distance behind the scrimmage line [length, yards], 25 yd default, 30 yd when opponents have a kick from running formation he cannot handle at 25 (printed, PDF p.253). The argmin-max is the Chebyshev-center / 1-center over the reachable threat set; the 25/30 yard depths are printed numbers, the minimax objective is the labeled formalization of 'nearest central spot to all the things which may happen'.
primitives.assumptions: Source prints prose coaching doctrine, no equations anywhere in the file; the LaTeX is a faithful predicate-logic / qualitative formalization of the printed decision rule, explicitly labeled as a formalization, not a source equation. Chapter XXX 'Punting - the Run-back' (PDF p.253 = printed p.235). Printed positioning doctrine: the fullback's regular position is twenty-five yards from scrimmage, increased to thirty against a kick-from-running-formation he cannot handle at twenty-five, and thirty is also his distance on kick formations against average kickers under normal wind and sun (PDF p.253). When alone in the backfield he inclines toward the center of the field; if the ball is scrimmaged fifteen yards from the side line he plays twenty-five to thirty yards from the side lines (PDF p.253). As his own goal line nears, his liability against long punts decreases and his duties merge into halfback / rushline duties (PDF p.253-254). The 'nearest central spot' sentence is the covering objective; the minimax form is its faithful formalization.
primitives.breakdown_regime: The minimax cover is over the REACHABLE threat set only - threats outside his line or beyond his arrival time are excluded by F, so the invariant is a constrained 1-center, not a global one; mis-specifying Theta_reach (e.g. ignoring a kick-from-running-formation) leaves the chosen spot exposed, which is exactly why the depth adapts 25->30. It breaks down when the threat distribution is misread (a placer who can directionally punt forces the fullback to the wide side, PDF p.252) or when the fullback is drawn into rushline duty near the goal and the covering role dissolves. The objective is robust (worst-case) rather than expected-value; a kicker who reliably lands in one zone would be better served by a weighted centroid, so the minimax form is a conservative doctrine, not a unique optimum.
timescales: tau_2: field-position battle across the game
tau_3: seasonal scouting of opponent kickers

layer2.mapping: Derived robust-covering kernel for the deep-defender node of the 22-player system: position is the Chebyshev center of the reachable threat distribution, with an adaptive depth parameter triggered by a detected kick-from-running-formation. This is the general operator of minimax facility location under a feasibility constraint, and it binds as the positioning rule for any single-cover agent: choose the spot minimizing worst-case arrival distance over the threats you are responsible for and can reach. The 25->30 yard adaptation is a regime switch in the kernel, the football instance of re-solving the covering problem when the threat model changes.
layer2.telemetry: Punt landing / threat-location distribution by formation; fullback depth and lateral position at the snap; run-back yards allowed and tackle arrival times; detected kick-from-running-formation frequency (the 25->30 trigger). The reachable-threat set Theta_reach is reconstructable from kick formation and fullback speed; the worst-case covering objective is a doctrine, so realized average outcomes need not match the minimax prediction.

primitives.name: Receiver self-determination + single-use interference invariant: the catcher chooses his own path; the helper is a budget-1 resource spent on the first/most dangerous down-field man
primitives.verbatim_quote: the second man in the backfield renders his best assistance by getting to the catcher, on either side, in time to assist in the receiving of the ball if fumbled, and, if the ball is caught, by eliminating the first man down the field who could spoil the runback if let alone.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Choose_catcher(path) vs Choose_other(path) = who selects the run-back path [decision-rights assignment]; the strict preference > formalizes the printed claim that a catcher advised by another 'is by no means as capable of warding off trouble' as one who chooses his own path (PDF p.255); Helper = the second backfield receiver [agent label]; Target = the down-field opponent the helper eliminates [agent label]; Threat(m) = how dangerous man m is to the run-back [ordinal, dimensionless]; argmax selects 'the first man down the field who could spoil the runback if let alone'; n_uses = number of decisive helper actions per kick [dimensionless count], bounded by 1 ('he can only feature and function once on each kick', PDF p.256). All terms are decision-rights assignments, agent labels, ordinal threats, or a dimensionless count; no physical units.
primitives.assumptions: Source prints prose coaching doctrine, no equations anywhere in the file; the LaTeX is a faithful predicate-logic / qualitative formalization of the printed decision rule, explicitly labeled as a formalization, not a source equation. Chapter XXX (PDF p.256 = printed p.238). Two printed invariants compose: (1) decision rights - 'The man who is advised as to his direction by another is by no means as capable of warding off trouble as the one who, having caught the ball, takes as much time as the circumstances allow, and then chooses his own path' (PDF p.255); a directed receiver 'is divided between his attempt to follow his teammate and his desire to bolt on his account'. (2) single-use helper - the second man renders best assistance by reaching the catcher in time to help on a fumble, and if caught, 'by eliminating the first man down the field who could spoil the runback if let alone'; 'By all means let him take out two or three of them if possible, but it is generally the case that he can only feature and function once on each kick' (PDF p.256). The helper's best path is straight up the field, blocking the most dangerous man in his path (PDF p.255).
primitives.breakdown_regime: The single-use budget is the binding constraint: a helper who spends his one decisive action on a low-threat man leaves the truly dangerous tackler free, so target selection (argmax Threat) is load-bearing, not the block count. The self-determination preference breaks down if the catcher lacks the skill/judgment to read converging tacklers - Cavanaugh concedes the catcher's best path is usually straight up the field and that stratagem (feigning position) is for experienced receivers (PDF p.257). The directed-receiver failure is a divided-attention / commitment problem, not a mere information deficit; supplying more advice does not fix it. The 'two or three if possible' clause is aspirational and does not relax the general budget-1 reality.
timescales: tau_0: the catch and first dodge (~1-2 s)
tau_3: season drill of receiver/helper assignments

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to decentralized decision rights plus single-use resource allocation to the maximum-threat target: the agent with the best local information (the catcher) holds the path decision, because centralizing it into a helper creates a divided-attention commitment loss; the helper is a budget-1 asset optimally spent on the highest-threat adversary, the football instance of allocating one indivisible resource to the max-weight target. In the engine this binds as a control-rights rule (local autonomy where local information dominates) coupled to a knapsack-of-one targeting kernel; a design that directs the catcher or spreads the helper across low-threat men is structurally dominated.
layer2.telemetry: Whether the catcher's path was self-chosen vs directed; helper's selected target and its threat rank; helper block success and whether a second decisive action occurred (budget violation); run-back yards and fumble-recovery assistance. The catcher's private read of converging tacklers is LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE except through the chosen path; threat ranking is reconstructable from down-field alignment and speed.

primitives.name: Placement-kick non-monotone block-hazard invariant: block danger peaks near eight yards depth; wing-block hazard rises with depth while line-collision hazard falls
primitives.verbatim_quote: At eight yards the danger probably is greatest, from that surge of blockers from the wings which, and which only, if his line be sound and properly coached, the kicker has to fear. Nearer than that, the danger of kicking into one's own line or opponents' increases directly just as the danger of a block from the sides decreases.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: d = kick depth behind the scrimmage line [length, yards]; h_block(d) = total probability the kick is blocked [dimensionless probability, 0-1]; h_wings(d) = block hazard from the surge of blockers from the wings [dimensionless probability, increasing in d]; h_line(d) = hazard of kicking into one's own or opponents' line [dimensionless probability, decreasing in d]; the up/down arrows formalize 'the danger of kicking into one's own line or opponents' increases directly just as the danger of a block from the sides decreases'; argmax_d h_block ~ 8 yd is the PRINTED peak ('At eight yards the danger probably is greatest'). No numeric hazard values are printed; the eight-yard peak is a sourced anchor, the additive competing-channel form is the labeled qualitative formalization.
primitives.assumptions: Source prints prose coaching doctrine, no equations anywhere in the file; the LaTeX is a faithful predicate-logic / qualitative formalization of the printed decision rule, explicitly labeled as a formalization, not a source equation. Chapter XXXI 'Drop Kick and Placement Kick' (PDF p.265 = printed p.247). Printed hazard structure: at fifteen yards the danger of a block 'begins to be felt'; at eight yards it 'probably is greatest, from that surge of blockers from the wings which, and which only, if his line be sound and properly coached, the kicker has to fear'; nearer than eight, line-collision danger rises as side-block danger falls (PDF p.265). This is why the placement kick is less dangerous than the drop kick close to scrimmage: 'Few drop-kickers dare attempt their specialty seven yards from scrimmage; fair placement kickers can attempt theirs from five' (PDF p.265). The placement kick is 'surer than the drop kick ... quicker, easier, and less likely to be blocked' (PDF p.266) because its angle of departure is controllable and it is faster off the foot. The non-monotone peak is the sovereign invariant.
primitives.breakdown_regime: The peak location (~8 yd) is conditioned on a sound, properly coached line - Cavanaugh's 'which, and which only' clause means a leaking line shifts or removes the interior maximum, so the invariant is line-quality-dependent, not universal. The two-channel additive form is a qualitative formalization; the true hazards may interact (a blocked wing rush changes line-collision risk), so h_block = h_wings + h_line is a first-order decomposition, not a printed identity. The doctrine favors placement over drop kicks, but he concedes more scores historically came from drop-kickers because there are 'a dozen drop-kickers for every place-kicker' (PDF p.266) - a base-rate / availability confound, not evidence against the per-attempt safety claim. No numeric probabilities are printed; the curve shape is the invariant, not its calibration.
timescales: tau_0: the kick and block rush (~1-2 s)
tau_3: era of drop-kick vs placement-kick prevalence

layer2.mapping: Derived competing-risk hazard kernel with an interior maximum for the kicking-depth decision node: two monotone hazard channels of opposite slope sum to a non-monotone total whose peak is an interior point (~8 yd), so the optimal kick depth is NOT at a boundary and a naive 'deeper is safer' or 'closer is safer' monotone rule is structurally wrong. This is the general operator of trade-off curves with interior optima (the football instance of a U-shaped / inverted-U risk function), and it binds as the depth-selection constraint plus the placement-vs-drop selector: the controllable-angle, faster placement kick dominates the drop kick in the close-to-scrimmage regime where line-collision hazard is high.
layer2.telemetry: Block rate by kick depth (the inverted-U is the testable signature); placement vs drop-kick success and block rates; line-quality proxy (pressure allowed) conditioning the peak; the printed eight-yard peak is the calibration anchor. Numeric hazard curves h_wings(d), h_line(d) are LATENT_UNIDENTIFIABLE from the source (no probabilities printed) and must be estimated from play-by-play, with the eight-yard peak as a soft constraint.

reasoning_traces.think: Begin with the resource and information structure Cavanaugh attacks in Chapter XXXIV. Zone play is a hard mapping from field position to a prescribed action: kick near your own goal, run twice then kick near midfield, conventional tactics inside the opponent forty. Cavanaugh's objection is not that the map is wrong in every cell but that it is a low-entropy policy an experienced defender can invert. He writes that the conservative style lets an experienced player on defense predict almost without failure what the opposing quarterback will elect to do. That is the core invariant: a predictable policy is an exploitable policy, and the exploit is free for the defense because it costs them nothing to read the zone. The deeper claim is about motive. Zone play persists, he argues, because coaches fear adverse criticism and distrust their field general's good sense, not because it maximizes winning. This is a principal-agent distortion stated in 1919 prose: the coach optimizes his reputation rather than the team's win probability, and the conservative map is the reputation-safe choice. The remedy has three parts, all printed: ungate the attack from the zone, start the strongest lineup, and score at the earliest feasible moment rather than saving dash for a final crash. The earliest-feasible-score rule is a timing invariant against the option-hoarding instinct; Cavanaugh notes a poor player is one whose strength does not increase as he nears a touchdown, so withholding the best runner until striking distance wastes the very resource that should be spent early. Now the decision kernel at the end of the chapter. When a first down is hazardous near scoring range, the quarterback chooses between a stroke for a touchdown and a try at field goal. The printed rule is a threshold plus a tie-break: take the field goal only if it seems slightly surer than the scoring play; if the chances are about even, take the big scoring play. Read structurally, this is payoff-dominance under near-equal probabilities: when p_FG and p_S are close, select the higher-payoff action (the touchdown), and only let the sure lower-payoff action win when its probability edge clears a 'slightly' margin. The margin is never numerically defined, so the invariant is the decision shape, not a calibrated boundary. An engine that always takes the field goal whenever p_FG exceeds p_S by any epsilon, or that maximizes expected points without the about-even tie-break, deviates from the doctrine. The two primitives together form a coherent generalship: raise policy entropy early, spend the best resources before the opponent's model converges, and resolve close scoring decisions by payoff dominance rather than by timidity.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The doctrine is scar tissue over a specific era. Cavanaugh contrasts his modern game with the old contest of two forty-five-minute halves, infrequent substitution, and possession considered four-fifths of the game, when men were kept in until practically exhausted and kicking was offense only with a strongly favoring wind. Zone play's energy-conservation rationale was born in that rugged, possession-scarce game; he argues it is an anachronism in the shorter, rest-intervaled modern game with clouds of substitutes and resubstitution. The hidden state in every modern conservative call is that older fear of collapse and of criticism, carried forward after the physical conditions that justified it had changed. His own career - the Denver Athletic Club, eighteen years of active coaching - is the empirical base he cites against the quitter label and against indiscriminate conservatism alike.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Three minds collide. The coach fears the newspaper verdict: a successful desperate pass is hailed as deception, the same play failed is proof of his lack of sense, so he self-represses toward the reputation-safe zone map. The quarterback holds the local information - the defensive spacing, the fullback playing short - and wants authority to use any play in his list when the defense modifies; Cavanaugh tells him he picks his own plays until he is positively wrong. The defensive coordinator across the field models the coach's conservatism and crowds his secondary within six yards, convinced no forward pass will be dared from the offense's own half. The exploit is a belief mismatch: the defense assumes zone play, the bold offense violates that assumption, and the coach's reputation fear is exactly what keeps the offense predictable enough for the defense's model to hold.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Higher layers veto the bold doctrine in specific states. Cavanaugh himself vetoes senseless indiscriminate offense and hap-hazard line pounding: each play must be planned so that, perfectly executed, it should score, so the judgment layer constrains the entropy prescription. The clock and nerve layer vetoes the very first aggressive snap: he concedes the opening kick may be justified by the wild first moment of panic, and that a long dangerous pass from a nervous center is its own risk. The kicking-game layer vetoes early offense when the team is genuinely inferior in kicking and lacks a favoring wind, because then the field-position externality dominates. The doctrine is a stance against timidity, not a license that overrides these physical and situational vetoes.

reasoning_traces.think: Three spatial invariants in the kicking game share one structure: constrain the adversary's options rather than guess them, and allocate scarce covering resources to the worst case. Start with the blocker. Cavanaugh's diagnosis of the failed kick-off block is precise: the blocker places himself directly in front of his charging opponent, who is thus enabled to force the blocker to two guesses as to the dodge direction. The remedy is to stay on one side of the man to be blocked and force him to the other side, collapsing the opponent's feasible evade set from two directions to one. This is a forcing move, not a prediction: instead of guessing left or right and losing half the time, the blocker removes the guess entirely by geometry. The same invariant recurs for blocking ends under punts - never let the end get directly in front of you; keep to one side so he has only a single direction in which to elude. The load-bearing condition is sincerity: the decisive lunge is reliable chiefly when the blocker knows the actual ball-carrier is directly behind him and must be protected, so the geometric constraint is coupled to an incentive constraint. Now the deep defender. The defensive fullback takes the nearest central spot to all the things which may happen which are in his line and which he can get. Read formally this is a constrained minimax cover: choose the position minimizing the worst-case distance over the reachable threat set, where reachable means within his responsibility and arrivable in time. It is a Chebyshev center, not a centroid, and it is restricted to threats he can actually get - a global cover would be wrong. The depth adapts from twenty-five to thirty yards when opponents reveal a kick from running formation he cannot handle at twenty-five, a regime switch in the covering problem when the threat model changes. Finally the receiver and his helper. The catcher must choose his own path, because a receiver advised by another is divided between following his teammate and bolting on his own account, and is less capable of warding off trouble. The helper is a budget-1 resource: he can only feature and function once on each kick, so his single decisive action must be spent eliminating the first and most dangerous down-field man who could spoil the runback if let alone. The unifying operator is choice-set reduction plus worst-case allocation of indivisible resources: force the opponent to one option, cover the worst reachable threat, and spend the one block on the max-threat target. A design that guesses instead of forces, covers the average instead of the worst case, or spreads the helper across low-threat men is structurally dominated.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: These invariants are products of the kicking-game-dominated 1919 field-position battle, when the punt exchange was the spine of the contest and the run-back was a neglected, nerve-shocking play. Cavanaugh repeatedly notes that coaches are content with a hazy confidence that they can run kick-offs back to the twenty or twenty-five, and that the kaleidoscopic broken field exerts a species of mesmerism on players who fail to act. The blocking and covering doctrine is scar tissue over that chaos: definite man-picking, one-side forcing, and a single decisive helper action are the institutional memory of teams that lost yards to frontal two-guess blocks and to helpers who spent their one block on the wrong man. The mini-gridiron and blackboard walk-through he proposes are the era's answer to the fatigue cost of live kick-off drill.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The blocker must model the charger's dodge while committing to one side; the charger reads the alignment and tries to force a two-way guess, so the block is a simultaneous-move game resolved by geometry rather than by reading. The catcher holds the best local information about converging tacklers and resents being directed, because advice splits his commitment; the helper who calls the path actually degrades the catcher's warding-off ability. The helper models which down-field man is most dangerous and knows he gets one decisive action, so he must rank threats before spending it. The coach models the blocker's sincerity problem: without the incentive of the runner directly behind, the Laodicean mental attitude returns and the lunge lacks conviction, so the coach's assignment design is itself a theory-of-mind intervention.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Geometry and physics veto the invariant when its preconditions fail. The single-side force assumes the blocker can hold his side and time the lunge; a faster opponent who reads the alignment beats a half-hearted block, so the geometric constraint is necessary but not sufficient and the sincerity layer vetoes a mechanically correct but uncommitted block. The covering kernel vetoes a mis-specified reachable-threat set: ignoring the kick-from-running-formation leaves the twenty-five-yard spot exposed, which is precisely why the depth must adapt. The single-use budget vetoes any helper plan that counts on two decisive blocks; the general reality is one, and a scheme built on taking out two or three men is aspirational, not admissible. The catcher-skill layer vetoes self-determination for a novice who cannot read converging tacklers, for whom the straight-up-field default is the safer constraint.

reasoning_traces.think: The placement-kick chapter contains a genuinely non-monotone risk invariant, and it is the most mathematically interesting doctrine in the book. Cavanaugh prints that at fifteen yards the danger of a block begins to be felt, that at eight yards it probably is greatest from the surge of blockers from the wings, and that nearer than eight the danger of kicking into one's own line or opponents' increases directly just as the danger of a block from the sides decreases. Decompose this into two competing hazard channels: a wing-block hazard that rises with kick depth, and a line-collision hazard that falls with depth. Their sum is non-monotone with an interior maximum near eight yards. The consequence is structural: the optimal kick depth is not at a boundary, and both naive monotone rules - deeper is safer, closer is safer - are wrong. This is the football instance of a trade-off curve with an interior optimum, an inverted-U risk function, and it is sovereign because the peak location is printed rather than invented. The peak is conditioned on a sound, properly coached line: Cavanaugh's which-and-which-only clause means a leaking line shifts or removes the interior maximum, so the invariant is line-quality-dependent. The same chapter yields the placement-versus-drop selector. The placement kick is surer, quicker, easier, and less likely to be blocked because its angle of departure is controllable and it is faster off the foot; close to scrimmage, where line-collision hazard is high, the placement kick dominates, and fair placement kickers can attempt from five yards where few drop-kickers dare seven. Cavanaugh is careful about a confound: more scores historically came from drop-kickers, but only because there are a dozen drop-kickers for every place-kicker - a base-rate and availability effect, not evidence against the per-attempt safety claim. The drop-kicker develops himself solo as a schoolboy with a tree or barn for a goal, while the placement kick requires a willing holder whose inglorious role breeds boredom; the cultural prevalence of drop-kicking is an incentive artifact, not a performance verdict. Stepping back, the book's mental doctrine ties the physical invariants together. Courage is never physical but always mental, so the physical giant produces no more courage than the pigmy, and even Achilles was not brave every day. The H-Hour chapter schedules arousal: it is a great mistake to arouse and excite players before every contest; reserve the oratory for the greater occasions, because repeated emotional stimulus habituates and cheapens the final appeal. The unifying lens is that football outcomes are governed by interior optima and by mental resource scheduling, not by monotone effort: there is a best kick depth, a best moment to score, a best moment to arouse, and pushing any of them to a boundary destroys value.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The drop-kick's cultural dominance is scar tissue over individualist romance: a boy and a football and a few newspaper headlines for inspiration, a tree or barn for a goal, develop the drop-kicker early and solo, while the placement kick needs a holder who shares the credit and whose role is inglorious. Cavanaugh notes most coaches secretly abhor both kickers because reliance on them weakens the rushing spirit and may force a team to depend on that scoring method. The hidden state in the modern kicking game is that older romantic individualism and the coach's fear of a kicking-dependent offense, which together suppressed the technically superior placement kick long after its per-attempt safety was understood. The mental doctrine - courage as mental, arousal as a reserved resource - is the era's psychology before sport science quantified it.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The kicker's apprehension about blocking is more acute on drop and place kicks than on punts because these attempts so seldom occur and so decisively bear on the outcome, so he needs to receive the pass only when he has signified preparedness; the abominable custom of opening his hands as the signal precipitates an immediate, often slightly-offside charge that blocks the kick. The holder models his own inglorious role and the boredom or rebellion it breeds, yet shares not a little in the credit of achievement. The coach models the team's rushing spirit and fears that a reliable kicker will make the offense timid and kicking-dependent. The center, hardened from of old to neglect and oblivion, deserves a third share of the credit that history records only for the kicker. Each mind optimizes a different projection of the same scoring attempt.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: The competing-risk structure vetoes monotone depth rules: a model that reads deeper-is-safer or closer-is-safer into the kick is fabricating a boundary optimum where the printed doctrine has an interior peak near eight yards. The line-quality layer vetoes treating the peak as universal; a leaking line removes the which-and-which-only condition and shifts the maximum, so the kernel must be conditioned on protection quality. The base-rate layer vetoes inferring per-attempt inferiority of the placement kick from aggregate scoring counts, because the dozen-to-one prevalence of drop-kickers confounds the comparison. The mental/arousal layer vetoes spending the emotional stimulus early and repeatedly: habituation cheapens the final appeal, so the H-Hour scheduling constraint reserves peak arousal for the supreme occasion, and a coach who excites before every contest has exhausted the resource before it matters.

universal_lens: The polymath audit lens this book trains is interior-optimum-and-choice-set thinking: decompose any competitive system into (1) the adversary's feasible action set and whether your alignment forces it to a singleton or leaves it a two-way guess, (2) the reachable threat set and whether your covering resource sits at its worst-case center, (3) the competing risk channels whose sum has an interior rather than boundary optimum, and (4) the mental and arousal resources that habituate if spent early. Cavanaugh's 1919 doctrine is a fossil record of these structures stated as prose decision rules; the audit asks of any proposed advantage which layer it lives in and whether a higher-priority layer vetoes it.
gsi_mapping: This book contains no biophysics, so the GSI transfer is explicitly structural, not sourced physiology: the single-side forcing invariant is isomorphic to constraining a patient's or adversary's option set before intervention rather than predicting their response; the nearest-central-spot covering kernel maps to robust triage positioning over the reachable worst-case deterioration set; the budget-1 helper maps to allocating one indivisible clinical resource to the highest-threat target; the non-monotone block-hazard maps to competing-risk dose curves with an interior optimum; and courage-as-mental plus H-Hour arousal scheduling map to habituation-aware psychological load management. Fluid, axonal-shear, and metabolic primitives must come from physiology sources, not this one.
gse_mapping: For the Coach-Mind simulator: implement the anti-zone-play entropy stance and earliest-feasible-score timing as opening-drive policy constraints; the field-goal-vs-scoring-play threshold plus payoff-dominance tie-break as a scoring-region decision kernel with a tunable, era-tagged 'slightly' margin; the single-side forcing invariant as a spatial constraint pruning any block alignment that leaves the opponent two free directions; the nearest-central-spot minimax cover with adaptive 25-to-30-yard depth as the deep-defender positioning kernel; the budget-1 helper as a knapsack-of-one max-threat targeting rule with catcher decision rights preserved; and the non-monotone block-hazard as the kick-depth and placement-vs-drop selector. Deception surfaces: model the defense's zone-play assumption, the frontal two-guess block leak, and the directed-receiver commitment loss. Internal artifacts only; no odds inputs; nothing published from this lane.
